_library.edition: ASME B94.9 ground-thread tap shank and square dimensions, as a maker publishes them for spiral point taps (machine screw sizes #6 to #10, fractional sizes 1/4 to 1/2); ISO 529:1975 shank diameter x square table (M3 to M12)
_library.source: Inch rows: the diameter-of-shank and size-of-square columns of the ground-thread tap tables of ICS Cutting Tools, 'Tap-Dimensions.pdf' (www.icscuttingtools.com/pdfs/Tap-Dimensions.pdf), which carry the ASME B94.9 figures; the ANSI table of 'Tap Shank Dimensions' in Enco's technical information sheet gives the same pairs (0.141x0.110, 0.168x0.131, 0.194x0.152, 0.255x0.191, 0.318x0.238, 0.381x0.286, 0.323x0.242, 0.367x0.275). Metric rows: the 'Tap Shank Dimensions ISO 529 - 1975' table of that Enco sheet (www.sme.in/enco/Tap shank diameter & square sizes for DIN and other Taps.pdf), dia. x square in mm. Where ISO 529 lists a size in its plain metric column the row says series 'plain'; M3 appears only in the shank-diameter-enlarged column, so its row says series 'enlarged'. A fractional tap from 7/16 up has a shank smaller than its thread: that is the standard's own figure, not an error
